newsitem.title: JAPAN: Tokyo stocks seen consolidating after recent gains.
newsitem.headline: Tokyo stocks seen consolidating after recent gains.

text.p: Tokyo stocks are likely to consolidate on Wednesday, as market participants take short-term profits after major gains on the previous day, brokers said.
But investor demand is expected to remain firm and this will limit any losses, they added.

On Tuesday, the 225-share Nikkei average surged 666.17 points or 3.41 percent to 20,180.92, the second largest point rise in the calendar year and the highest closing level since the 20,413.46 level reached on December 17.
June Nikkei futures rose 660 points to 20,190.
Brokers expect the Nikkei 225 to hover between 19,900 and 20,500.
"The underlying tone will still be firm, but it is very likely that stocks will take a breather today," said Kenji Karikomi, a deputy general manager at Daiwa Securities Co Ltd.
Tuesday's surge in the Nikkei 225 shows signs of overheating on technical charts, he said.
"Traders may take profits, but even if selling orders are heavy, they will be absorbed by buying from foreign investors and pension funds," said an analyst at a foreign securities house.
A fall in the Nasdaq index overnight in New York might depress Japanese high-technology issues, the analyst said.
On Tuesday, the Nasdaq composite finished down about 11 points, or 0.82 percent, at 1,328. The Dow industrials gained 11 points to close at 7,225.
Some investors said the market lacked factors to inspire further buying above the key 20,000 line.

"Foreign investors (who have bought Japanese stocks recently) are basically seeking laggards, such as in the shipbuilding sector. There was no active buying to chase the upside of major blue-chip shares," said a portfolio manager at a securities investment advisory firm.
By sector, gainers were led by brokerages, shipbuilding, transport equipment and warehousing. The major losing sectors were railway/bus, foods, credit/lease and rubber.
